decisions.reason: As a modular relaunch of an already well-liked trommel screen, it builds directly on the firm's existing screening know-how and installed-base learning, so management would be very unlikely to withdraw it soon.

A mobile high-speed flail shredder is close to the firm's core mobile processing machinery capabilities, and having its own product page suggests enough commitment and absorptive capacity to refine it rather than exit quickly.

The mobile high-speed grinder fits the firm's adjacent knowledge base in mobile waste and biomass processing, but its lighter website presence implies somewhat less proven traction and therefore a moderate, not high, withdrawal risk.

A stationary electric fine shredder matches the firm's move toward tougher and more resource-efficient processing solutions, and its engineering, service, and R&D base should allow continued improvement despite early-market uncertainty.

The green-waste-specific mobile grinder is technically related to the firm's core business but serves a narrower application niche, so management would likely keep it for further learning while accepting a somewhat higher risk of discontinuation.

Stationary single-shaft pre-shredders are strongly aligned with the firm's established shredding and plant business, and the dedicated presentation indicates a deliberate strategic extension that management would be unlikely to reverse within a year.
